chunks: And the Sheikh (may God the Exalted support him) informed me, saying: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Aban, from 'Anbasa — who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
'Ali (peace be upon him) did not consider wudu obligatory for al-madhy, nor washing what of it touched the garment — except in the case of the major water (janaba/ghusl).'

key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْأَكْبَرِ: al-ma' al-akbar: 'the greater/major water' — classical technical term for janaba (major ritual impurity) requiring ghusl, contrasted with the minor impurity requiring wudu (al-ma' al-asghar)
key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: al-madhy: pre-ejaculatory fluid emitted during sexual arousal, distinct from maniy (semen); its ritual status differs markedly between Shia and Sunni schools
key_terms.غَسْلَ: ghasala/ghusl (wash): here refers to washing the garment; the exception in 'al-ma' al-akbar' implies that during janaba the garment must be washed
key_terms.وُضُوءًا: wudu: the minor ritual ablution required before salat and other acts of worship; the hadith rules that al-madhy does not nullify it

ai.seo_question: Does al-madhy (pre-seminal fluid) nullify wudu or require washing clothes in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reports that Imam Ali (AS) held al-madhy (the thin pre-ejaculatory fluid emitted during sexual arousal) to be neither a breaker of wudu nor a source of obligation to wash the clothes it contacts. The sole exception is the state of major ritual impurity (janaba), where ghusl is already required and implicitly covers any accompanying najasah. This reflects the dominant Shia jurisprudential view: al-madhy is a minor impurity that does not nullify wudu, in contrast to the opinion of some other legal schools.
